arxiv-2102-07226.title: An Efficient Forecasting Approach to Reduce Boundary Effects in Real-Time Time-Frequency Analysis
arxiv-2102-07226.creator: Adrien Meynard, Hau-Tieng Wu
arxiv-2102-07226.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Adrien Meynard, Hau-Tieng Wu. Time-frequency (TF) representations of time series are intrinsically subject to the boundary effects. As a result, the structures of signals that are highlighted by the representations are garbled when approaching the boundaries of the TF domain. In this paper, for the purpose of real-time TF information acquisition of nonstationary oscillatory time series, we propose a numerically efficient approach for the reduction of such boundary effects. The solution relies on an extension of the analyzed signal obtained by a forecasting technique.

arxiv-2105-10863.title: Selberg’s Central limit theorem for quadratic dirichlet L-functions over function fields
arxiv-2105-10863.creator: Pranendu Darbar, Allysa Lumley
arxiv-2105-10863.description: Abstract . In this article, we study the logarithm of the central value L ⁡ ( 1 2 , χ D ) L\left(\frac{1}{2},\chi_{D}\right) in the symplectic family of Dirichlet L L -functions associated with the hyperelliptic curve of genus δ \delta over a fixed finite field 𝔽 q \mathbb{F}_{q} in the limit as δ → ∞ \delta\to\infty .

arxiv-2106-12718.title: Sparse Flows: Pruning Continuous-depth Models
arxiv-2106-12718.creator: Lucas LiebenweinMIT CSAIL lucas@csail.mit.edu, Ramin HasaniMIT CSAIL rhasani@mit.edu Alexander AminiMIT CSAIL amini@mit.edu Daniela RusMIT CSAIL rus@csail.mit.edu
arxiv-2106-12718.description: Abstract Continuous deep learning architectures enable learning of flexible probabilistic models for predictive modeling as neural ordinary differential equations (ODEs), and for generative modeling as continuous normalizing flows. In this work, we design a framework to decipher the internal dynamics of these continuous depth models by pruning their network architectures.

arxiv-2109-04765.title: Surfactant-driven instability of a divergent flow
arxiv-2109-04765.creator: G. Koleski, J.-C. Loudet, A. Vilquin, B. Pouligny, T. Bickel
arxiv-2109-04765.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by G. Koleski, J.-C. Loudet, A. Vilquin, B. Pouligny, T. Bickel. Extremely small amounts of surface-active contaminants are known to drastically modify the hydrodynamic response of the water-air interface. Surfactant concentrations as low as a few thousand molecules per square micron are sufficient to eventually induce complete stiffening. In order to probe the shear response of a water-air interface, we design a radial flow experiment that consists in an upward water jet directed to the interface.

arxiv-2110-12566.title: Three circle theorem on almost Hermitian manifolds and applications Thanks: 1 Research partially supported by GDNSF with contract no. 2021A1515010264 and NNSF of China with contract no. 11571215.
arxiv-2110-12566.creator: Chengjie Yu 1, Chuangyuan Zhang
arxiv-2110-12566.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Chengjie Yu 1, Chuangyuan Zhang. In this paper, we extend Gang Liu’s three circle theorem for Kähler manifolds to almost Hermitian manifolds. As applications of the three circle theorem, we obtain sharp dimension estimates for spaces of holomorphic functions of polynomial growth and rigidity for the estimates, Liouville theorems for pluri-subharmonic functions of sub-logarithmic growth and Liouville theorems for holomorphic functions of Cheng-type, and fundamental theorem of algebra on almost Hermitian manifolds with slightly negative holomorphic sectional curvature.

arxiv-2112-06486.title: Prediction in functional regression with discretely observed and noisy covariates
arxiv-2112-06486.creator: Siegfried Hörmann
arxiv-2112-06486.description: Abstract In practice functional data are sampled on a discrete set of observation points and often susceptible to noise. We consider in this paper the setting where such data are used as explanatory variables in a regression problem. If the primary goal is prediction, we show that the gain by embedding the problem into a scalar-on-function regression is limited.

arxiv-2208-13600.title: Towards Robust Face Recognition with Comprehensive Search
arxiv-2208-13600.creator: Manyuan Zhang, Guanglu Song, Yu Liu †, Hongsheng Li
arxiv-2208-13600.description: Abstract Data cleaning, architecture, and loss function design are important factors contributing to high-performance face recognition. Previously, the research community tries to improve the performance of each single aspect but failed to present a unified solution on the joint search of the optimal designs for all three aspects.

arxiv-2402-17226.title: Reasoning in Conversation: Solving Subjective Tasks through Dialogue Simulation for Large Language Models
arxiv-2402-17226.creator: Xiaolong Wang, Yile Wang, Yuanchi Zhang, Fuwen Luo, Peng Li, Maosong Sun, Yang Liu
arxiv-2402-17226.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable performance in objective tasks such as open-domain question answering and mathematical reasoning, which can often be solved through recalling learned factual knowledge or chain-of-thought style reasoning. However, we find that the performance of LLMs in subjective tasks is still unsatisfactory, such as metaphor recognition, dark humor detection, etc.

arxiv-2502-02492.title: VideoJAM: Joint Appearance-Motion Representations for Enhanced Motion Generation in Video Models
arxiv-2502-02492.creator: Hila Chefer, Uriel Singer, Amit Zohar, Yuval Kirstain, Adam Polyak, Yaniv Taigman, Lior Wolf, Shelly Sheynin
arxiv-2502-02492.description: Abstract Despite tremendous recent progress, generative video models still struggle to capture real-world motion, dynamics, and physics. We show that this limitation arises from the conventional pixel reconstruction objective, which biases models toward appearance fidelity at the expense of motion coherence.

arxiv-2502-11513.title: MaZO: Masked Zeroth-Order Optimization for Multi-Task Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
arxiv-2502-11513.creator: Zhen Zhang, Yifan Yang, Kai Zhen, Nathan Susanj, Athanasios Mouchtaris, Siegfried Kunzmann, Zheng Zhang
arxiv-2502-11513.description: Abstract Large language models have demonstrated exceptional capabilities across diverse tasks, but their fine-tuning demands significant memory, posing challenges for resource-constrained environments. Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization provides a memory-efficient alternative by eliminating the need for backpropagation. However, ZO optimization suffers from high gradient variance, and prior research has largely focused on single-task learning, leaving its application to multi-task learning unexplored.

arxiv-2508-03431.title: A Note on The Rationale Behind Using Parental Longevity as a Proxy in Mendelian Randomization Studies
arxiv-2508-03431.creator: Zach Shahn, Rehana Rasul, Mary Schooling
arxiv-2508-03431.description: Abstract In many cohorts (such as the UK Biobank ( Sudlow et al., 2015 ) ) on which Mendelian Randomization (MR) studies are routinely performed, data on participants’ longevity is inadequate as the majority of participants are still living. To nevertheless estimate effects on longevity, it is increasingly common for researchers to substitute participants’ ‘parental attained age’, i.e.

arxiv-2509-14126.title: CrazyMARL: Decentralized Direct Motor Control Policies for Cooperative Aerial Transport of Cable-Suspended Payloads
arxiv-2509-14126.creator: Viktor Lorentz, Khaled Wahba, Sayantan Auddy, Marc Toussaint, Wolfgang Hönig
arxiv-2509-14126.description: Abstract Collaborative transportation of cable-suspended payloads by teams of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs)has the potential to enhance payload capacity, adapt to different payload shapes, and provide built-in compliance, making it attractive for applications ranging from disaster relief to precision logistics. However, multi-UAVcoordination under disturbances, nonlinear payload dynamics, and slack–taut cable modes remains a challenging control problem.

arxiv-2601-03226.title: Generalized affine buildings for semisimple algebraic groups over real closed fields Thanks: Address : Department of Mathematics, Heidelberg University, Germany Thanks: E-mail : rappenzeller@mathi.uni-heidelberg.de
arxiv-2601-03226.creator: Raphael Appenzeller
arxiv-2601-03226.description: Abstract . We use real algebraic geometry to construct an affine Λ \Lambda -building ℬ \mathcal{B} associated to the 𝔽 \mathbb{F} -points of a semisimple algebraic group, where 𝔽 \mathbb{F} is a valued real closed field. We characterize the spherical building at infinity and the local building at a base point.

johnson-dictionary-english-language-1755.creator: Samuel Johnson
johnson-dictionary-english-language-1755.description: Johnson's Dictionary of the English Language, vol. 1 (A–K), from the 1756 second edition of the 1755 first — the landmark English dictionary: definitions, etymologies, and illustrative quotations that set the standard for a century.

pmc-10671925.title: Spontaneous Cultural Conversion Rate of Mycobacterium avium Complex Pulmonary Disease Based on BACES Severity
pmc-10671925.creator: Bo-Guen Kim, Jin Young Yu, Byung Woo Jhun, Ana Lopez-de-Andres, Hiroshi Ishii
pmc-10671925.description: Background: Only a few clinical factors can aid in predicting spontaneous culture conversion (SCC) in patients with Mycobacterium avium complex-pulmonary disease (MAC-PD). In this study, we aimed to evaluate whether the rate of SCC varies according to the severity of the disease in MAC-PD patients.

pmc-10708896.title: Potential Use of ChatGPT for Patient Information in Periodontology: A Descriptive Pilot Study
pmc-10708896.creator: Osman Babayiğit, Zeynep Tastan Eroglu, Dilek Ozkan Sen, Fatma Ucan Yarkac
pmc-10708896.description: ObjectivesThe aim of this study is to evaluate the accuracy and completeness of the answers given by Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer (ChatGPT) (OpenAI OpCo, LLC, San Francisco, CA), to the most frequently asked questions on different topics in the field of periodontology.

pmc-10714202.title: Bandgap engineering of germanene for gas sensing applications†
pmc-10714202.creator: Ong Kim Le, Viorel Chihaia, Do Ngoc Son
pmc-10714202.description: Gas sensors are used to detect gas components in human breath to diagnose diseases, such as cancers. However, choosing suitable two-dimensional materials for gas sensors is a challenge. Germanene can be a good candidate because of its outstanding electronic and structural properties.

pmc-11517464.title: Exploring anxiety and depression trends: insights from the BELHEALTH cohort 2022-2024 in Belgium
pmc-11517464.creator: C Duveau, L Hermans, H Bruggeman, G Nélis, R Charafeddine, M Dispas, S Demarest, L Gisle
pmc-11517464.description: BackgroundThe swift impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and ensuing restrictions on the mental health of the Belgian population prompted the need for a sustainable system to monitor its evolution. Repeated COVID-19 surveys were conducted between 2020 and 2022 to address this issue, followed by the launch of the BELHEALTH cohort project.

pmc-11544824.title: Oral Nutritional Supplementation in Older Adults with a Hip Fracture—Findings from a Bi-National Clinical Audit
pmc-11544824.creator: Jack J. Bell, Rebecca J. Mitchell, Ian A. Harris, Hannah Seymour, Elizabeth Armstrong, Roger Harris, Stewart Fleming, Sarah Hurring, Jacqueline Close
pmc-11544824.description: Background/Objectives: Evidence-based guidelines and care standards recommend offering oral nutrition supplements to all older adults with hip fracture, not just those already malnourished. This study aimed to identify the proportion of inpatients in a sample of hospitals in two countries that were provided with oral nutritional supplementation (ONS) following a hip fracture and to identify factors associated with ONS provision.

pmc-12462297.title: Dissecting the genetic architecture of circadian rhythms in human tissues using a quantitative circadian deviation score
pmc-12462297.creator: Zheyu Li, Liang Chen
pmc-12462297.description: BackgroundCircadian rhythms influence various physiological and behavioral processes, including sleep, metabolism, and immune response. Although key regulatory factors of biological clocks have been identified and genome-wide association studies have pinpointed some genetic variants linked to sleep traits, the genetic architecture underlying circadian rhythms remains incompletely understood.

pmc-12528241.title: Low tumour burden is associated with observation after surgery in patients with grade 2 astrocytoma and oligodendroglioma: results from the prospective multicentre LoG-Glio registry
pmc-12528241.creator: Andreas Ziebart, Julia Onken, Minou Nadji-Ohl, Christine Jungk, Stefan Rückriegel, Dorothee Mielke, Rüdiger Gerlach, Marie-Therese Forster, Constantin Roder, Katja Kniese, Nicolas Neidert, Ludovica Fabbrocini, Darius Kalasauskas, Gerges Aziz, Sabrina Riehl, Lennart Sannwald, Benjamin Mayer, Christia
pmc-12528241.description: PurposeRecent evidence-based guidelines recommend adjuvant therapy following surgery for most patients with WHO grade 2 and 3 gliomas. However, deviations from these recommendations are frequently observed in clinical practice. This study aimed to evaluate patterns of postoperative management across Germany, using multicentre registry data from certified neuro-oncology centres.

pmc-12553247.title: Resilience among clinical pharmacists and related factors: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12553247.creator: Yusuke Tsuchiya, Wataru Arai, Nobuko Sunami, Hiroyuki Hosono, Tae Maeshima, Fumio Itagaki, Machiko Watanabe
pmc-12553247.description: BackgroundResilience has recently attracted attention as a means of coping with challenging situations. Although there have been several studies on resilience among healthcare professionals, there are limited reports on resilience among pharmacists. In this study, we conducted a survey of resilience among clinical pharmacists and examined factors related to self-efficacy, burnout, and work.

pmc-12606338.title: Engineered CXCR3-A expression enhances B7-H3-targeting CAR T cell migration and efficacy against diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
pmc-12606338.creator: Edward Z. Song, Andrea Timpanaro, Michael Meechan, Leonel Elena-Sanchez, Lucy Z. Li, Sophie Jamet, Davina S. Lau, Lily I. Winter, Matthew D. Dun, Jessica B. Foster, Myron K. Evans, Siobhan S. Pattwell, Vandana Kalia, Surojit Sarkar, Michael C. Jensen, Matthew C. Biery, Nicholas A. Vitanza
pmc-12606338.description: Diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG) is a fatal brainstem tumor desperately in need of better treatments. Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapies for DIPG have demonstrated clinical tolerability and bioactivity, but not universal benefit. A major obstacle is insufficient CAR T cell trafficking to the tumor.

pmc-12611639.title: Circulation of polyclonal OXA-244-producing Escherichia coli lineages in Jerusalem, Israel
pmc-12611639.creator: Janko Sattler, Yonatan Oster, Helena M B Seth Smith, Yukino Gütlin, Ayelet Michael-Gayego, Dan Reshef, Violeta Temper, Karsten Borgwardt, Adrian Egli, Jacob Strahilevitz, Jacob Moran-Gilad
pmc-12611639.description: Background and objectivesOXA-244-producing Escherichia coli represents an emerging concern in Europe due to its rapid spread and difficult-to-detect phenotype. While other OXA-48-like carbapenemases emerged in Israel in 2007, the circulation of OXA-244-producing E. coli was only recently reported. We aimed to investigate the proportion of OXA-244 amongst OXA-48-like-producing E.

pmc-12698816.title: pSOFA score serves as predicting the severity and outcome of sepsis in critically ill children
pmc-12698816.creator: Li-dan Zhang, Li Wang, Yu-hui Wu, Hong-xin Lin, Xing Nie, Ye-qin Xu, Wen Tang, Yu-xiong Guo, Yu-cai Cheng
pmc-12698816.description: To investigate the prognostic value of the Pediatric Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (pSOFA) in children with sepsis during hospitalization. Clinical data for children with sepsis or severe sepsis hospitalized in the PICU of the First Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University and that of Shenzhen Children’s Hospital from December 2014 to December 2019 were retrospectively analyzed.

pmc-12953265.title: Pediatric H3 G34-mutant diffuse hemispheric glioma: clinical, imaging and molecular prognostic factors, MGMT expression, and temozolomide response
pmc-12953265.creator: Dana Tlais, Qunyu Zhang, Jordan T. Roach, Christopher L. Tinkle, Tong Lin, Xiaoyu Li, Ayatullah Mostafa, Daniel C. Moreira, Rene Y. McNall-Knapp, Sarah Z. Rush, Brian H. Le, Sara Sinno, Apeksha Ramnarayan, Kevin F. Ginn, Sonia Partap, Arzu Onar-Thomas, Larissa V. Furtado, Asim K. Bag, Jason Chiang
pmc-12953265.description: Previous studies have demonstrated poor outcomes in pediatric patients with H3 G34-mutant diffuse hemispheric glioma (DHG). However, the biological basis for this therapeutic resistance remains poorly understood. Furthermore, the effectiveness of temozolomide (TMZ) and the role of surgery in pediatric patients remain uncertain.

pmc-13080762.title: Screening the Chemical Composition, Antioxidant Activity, and Toxicity of Ten Species of Non‐Conventional Food Plants From Southern Brazil
pmc-13080762.creator: Luana Vanessa Peretti Minello, Paola Dutra da Rosa, Sabrina dos Santos Cassol, Luciana Bavaresco Andrade Touguinha, Cátia Santos Branco, Valdirene Camatti Sartori
pmc-13080762.description: Non‐conventional food plants (NCFPs) are resilient, adaptable species with nutritional qualities. Brazil has the world's greatest biodiversity in these species. Despite evidence of their potential for sustainable nutrition, there are few related studies. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the antioxidant capacity, total polyphenol content, main compounds, and in vivo toxicity of ten NCFPs from southern Brazil.

pmc-13291227.creator: Yuyu Liu, Guanchen Bai, Xingli Zhao, Xiaohui Suo, Yanliang Bai, Fang Zheng, Weihua Zhao, Hongling Peng, Dongmei Wang, Liyun Zhao, Jie Liu, Ling Li, Zeping Zhou, Yingchang Mi, Kaiqi Liu

pmc-13629813.creator: Lijun Sun, Mengna Ruan, Ziyu Liu, Xiaojing Tang, Lin Li, Senyan Liu

pmc-13655252.title: Multi‐Omics Integration Reveals Metabolic Reprogramming and EMT‐Driven Metastasis in Triple‐Negative Breast Cancer
pmc-13655252.creator: Yuheng Pang, Yuefeng Shang, Wenjing Wang, Tong Liu, Xiaolong Zou
pmc-13655252.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Triple‐negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive subtype with high metastatic potential and poor prognosis, yet the molecular mechanisms driving metastasis remain incompletely understood. Here, we performed integrated transcriptomic, metabolomic, and imaging mass cytometry (IMC) analyses on tumor tissues from 52 TNBC patients stratified into NonMeta (long‐term survival without metastasis, n = 39) and MetaPoor (metastasis‐related death within 36 months after metastatic diagnosis, n = 13) groups.
